AddContactRequest.description:
Slice 4 (docs/plans/2026-09-05-contacts-stats/spec.md §Tool contracts).

No length/shape constraints declared here (unlike ``SaveArtifactRequest``'s
``label``): every cap is a live ``settings`` value a test can monkeypatch,
so ``contacts.add_contact`` checks them at call time — the same pattern
``SaveFitRequest.clamp_reasoning``/``RecordEventRequest.clamp_detail`` use.
``added_by`` is deliberately ABSENT — ``extra="forbid"`` rejects it (S2).
AddContactRequest.title: AddContactRequest

AddContactsBatchRequest.title: AddContactsBatchRequest

AddPersonRequest.description:
``POST /api/contacts`` — a job-less (cold) contact when
``application_id`` is omitted, a linked one otherwise (owner decision,
2026-09-25). Kept as a SEPARATE model from ``AddContactRequest`` (used by
the per-application route, where the id comes off the URL) so that route
keeps refusing an ``application_id`` in its body (S3 — the id there is
never caller-supplied).
AddPersonRequest.title: AddPersonRequest

AgentEditOut.description:
One live ASSISTANT edit on ``GET /profile``'s ``agent_edits``.

``previous_value`` is the field's base value — what the CV / the user's
own saves hold under this edit, and so exactly what "Take back" restores
(the label never promises a value Take back would not produce).
``None`` / ``""`` / ``[]`` all mean "it was empty" — the page words them
that way.
AgentEditOut.title: AgentEditOut

AlignmentOut.description:
``GET …/alignment`` (2026-09-20) — the fit picture: the agent's stored
verdict beside which of the candidate's own skills occur in the stored
ad text. Two stored facts drawn together; nothing computed about the
candidate (VISION rule 4).
AlignmentOut.title: AlignmentOut

ApplicationArtifactOut.description:
The ``get_application`` artifacts-list shape: ``text`` is ALWAYS a key
(null unless ``with_artifact_text=true`` and under the byte cap).
ApplicationArtifactOut.title: ApplicationArtifactOut

ApplicationArtifactRowOut.description:
``get_application_artifact`` — one version in full. No ``truncated``:
this route always returns the real row, never a capped read.
ApplicationArtifactRowOut.title: ApplicationArtifactRowOut

ApplicationControlsOut.description:
The state behind the four human-in-the-loop buttons on the application
page, each with who / where / when, plus an open blocked record.
ApplicationControlsOut.title: ApplicationControlsOut

ApplicationEventOut.title: ApplicationEventOut

ApplicationKitOut.description:
Everything an assistant needs to fill ONE application form (S3). Binds to
THIS application only: its latest CV and cover letter, never another job's.
ApplicationKitOut.title: ApplicationKitOut

ApplicationReceiptOut.description:
``get_application``'s receipts list — never carries the receipt text
(that call site never passes ``include_text``; see
``ApplicationReceiptExportOut`` for the ``export_history`` shape).
ApplicationReceiptOut.title: ApplicationReceiptOut

ApplicationVisaOut.description:
Slice 7 — fact 1 (the agent's reading of the ad) plus the ONE
comparison against fact 2 (the candidate's countries). ``needs_sponsorship``
is ``null`` whenever either side is silent (rule #29).
ApplicationVisaOut.title: ApplicationVisaOut

ArtifactDiffBaseOut.description:
Slice 8 — what the target version is compared against: the profile's
stored CV (``profile``), another version of the same kind (``artifact``),
or nothing (``none`` — a first version of a non-cv kind).
ArtifactDiffBaseOut.title: ArtifactDiffBaseOut

ArtifactDiffOut.description:
``GET …/artifacts/{artifact_id}/diff`` — read-only; the web paints it.
``applied`` is the receipt's word, not a button's (VISION decision 26).
ArtifactDiffOut.title: ArtifactDiffOut

AssistantSettingsView.description:
The assistant settings, as the web and MCP ``get_profile`` read them.

``inbox_mode`` / ``check_every`` / ``notes`` are an ALIAS of
``preferences.daily_check`` / ``check_every`` / ``assistant_notes`` — shown
here, still edited at those paths.
AssistantSettingsView.title: AssistantSettingsView

AutoEmailCheckResponse.description:
``GET /api/applications/{id}/auto-email-check`` - the gate before an automatic employer email.
``send`` only means the gate is open; ``due_since`` is "" when the kind has no starting event.
AutoEmailCheckResponse.title: AutoEmailCheckResponse

BlockedSubmittedOut.description: "I submitted it": the new receipt's id plus the refreshed decision state.
BlockedSubmittedOut.title: BlockedSubmittedOut

CVDetail.description: Full extracted CV data for transparent display.
CVDetail.title: CVDetail

ContactEditOut.description:
One value a contact field has ever held — the base row's own value is
entry 0, oldest first, so ``[-1]`` is always current.
ContactEditOut.title: ContactEditOut

ContactOut.description:
A contact row (``contacts.list_contacts`` / ``add_contact``'s return).
Same shape everywhere a contact appears — detail, export, the add
response. ``application_id`` is ``null`` for a cold (job-less) contact
(owner decision, 2026-09-25). ``edit_history``/``outreach`` carry the
append-only overlays added the same day.
ContactOut.title: ContactOut

ControlsBlockedOut.description: S6: the assistant's open ``blocked`` record (no later ``unblocked``).
ControlsBlockedOut.title: ControlsBlockedOut

DoctorAuth.description:
How this caller is signed in: ``session`` (browser), ``token`` (personal
``j360_…`` token) or ``oauth`` (an OAuth-connected assistant), and the
actor string every event it records will carry.
DoctorAuth.title: DoctorAuth

DoctorAutoEmails.description:
Automatic employer emails, watched: the switch, today's count, the last sends (company, never the
address), what is due, and any send that broke a guardrail.
DoctorAutoEmails.title: DoctorAutoEmails

DoctorMissingItem.description: One thing the profile lacks: a path-like ``key`` and a plain ``why``.
DoctorMissingItem.title: DoctorMissingItem

DoctorOutreach.description:
Today's outreach (the user's own day): ``sent_today`` recorded sends,
``daily_max`` the cap check_outreach applies, ``blocked_today`` how many
check_outreach answers today were ``stop``.
DoctorOutreach.title: DoctorOutreach

DoctorResponse.description:
``GET /api/doctor`` - one read of "what state is this account in, and
what should the assistant do next?". Every field is built defensively: a
user with no profile gets ``profile_exists: false``, never a 404.

default.disclaimer: Elapsed time only — not legal advice or a claim that the employer did anything wrong.

DoctorResponse.title: DoctorResponse

DoctorSetup.description: The six-round setup: rounds done, of ``total``; ``next`` = first unfinished ("" when all done).
DoctorSetup.title: DoctorSetup

DoctorSilentBlock.description: Feedback loop slice 4: interviews with silence past ``courtesy_days`` (read-only).

disclaimer.default: Elapsed time only — not legal advice or a claim that the employer did anything wrong.
disclaimer.title: Disclaimer

DoctorSilentBlock.title: DoctorSilentBlock

DoctorSilentItem.description: One interview-stage application with no word since its last interview_done.
DoctorSilentItem.title: DoctorSilentItem

EventSource.description:
Slice 6 (docs/plans/2026-09-07-email-evidence/spec.md §Tool contracts)
— the email an event came from. No length caps declared here: every cap
is a live ``settings`` value ``spine.validate_source`` checks at call
time, the same reasoning ``AddContactRequest``'s docstring gives.
EventSource.title: EventSource

EventSourceOut.description:
Slice 6 — the ``source`` shape every reader emits (or ``null``, when
the event carries none).
EventSourceOut.title: EventSourceOut

ExportArtifactOut.description:
``export_history``'s artifact METADATA (not the full row): ``text`` is
only a key at all when ``include_text=true`` — hence the default.
ExportArtifactOut.title: ExportArtifactOut

FitAxisIn.description:
One axis of the fit picture (2026-09-20): the agent's own name for a
dimension and two 0..100 numbers — how much the role asks on it and how
much the seeker brings. Bounds on the count and the name length are live
settings checked by ``spine.validate_axes``.
FitAxisIn.title: FitAxisIn

FitItemIn.description:
One gap / ad requirement with an optional hard|soft marker (slice 5).
The kind set and the text cap are live settings checked by
``fit_record.clean_items`` (so a bad kind is a 422 naming the set).
FitItemIn.title: FitItemIn

FormCheckOut.description:
For every question on the live form: a saved answer from this application's
kit, or a gap to ask the user about. Job360 only looks up; the assistant reads
the form and decides.
FormCheckOut.title: FormCheckOut

FormCheckRequest.description: ``POST /applications/{id}/kit/form-check`` body: every question on the live form.
FormCheckRequest.title: FormCheckRequest

FormQuestion.description:
One question read off a LIVE application form. ``key`` is the kit key the
assistant plans to answer it with (``contact.email``, ``logistics.notice_period``,
or the saved ``approved_text`` question).
FormQuestion.title: FormQuestion

GrantScopeCount.description: How many applications, their distinct form hosts, and how many have no host yet.
GrantScopeCount.title: GrantScopeCount

GrantScopeOut.description:
Gap roadmap slice 30 - what an "Auto for a while" grant covers. ``queue``: what a grant
confirmed NOW would cover (the user's open queue; the confirm shows it). ``granted``: what the
grant in force covers (``None`` = no grant in force, or ``unscoped``). ``unscoped``: a grant from
before snapshots, covering every application until it ends.
GrantScopeOut.title: GrantScopeOut

InboxCheckedIn.description: The assistant read Gmail for these applications up to ``checked_at`` (now when empty).
InboxCheckedIn.title: InboxCheckedIn

InterviewAgenda.description:
``upcoming`` = live interviews in the next 7 days; ``just_passed`` = those of the last 3 days whose
application has no outcome event yet (ask the user how it went).
InterviewAgenda.title: InterviewAgenda

InterviewAgendaItem.description: One live interview in the agenda read (services/applications/agenda.py).
InterviewAgendaItem.title: InterviewAgendaItem

JobResponse.description:
The ad the user brought, exactly as it is stored.

Slice 5 (#483) took the score off this model. Job360 never judges fit
(product rule 4) — the user's own agent does, and records its verdict with
`save_fit`. Every field below is read straight off the `jobs` row; nothing
here is computed about the user.
JobResponse.title: JobResponse

JsonResumeResponse.description:
``GET /profile/json-resume`` body. Wraps the canonical JSON Resume
dict (https://jsonresume.org/schema/) under a ``resume`` key so the
response is a JSON object, not a bare list.
JsonResumeResponse.title: JsonResumeResponse

KitFileOut.description: A short-lived download link. The token is in ``url`` and exists nowhere else.
KitFileOut.title: KitFileOut

KitHoldOut.description:
Another assistant session is on this application (weak spot #3, 2026-10-15).
``session`` is the other holder's own label (data, never markup; ``""`` = none
given). ``unsure``: the caller passed no ``session`` and its own assistant read
the kit under a label - maybe another session of the same assistant (``detail``).
KitHoldOut.title: KitHoldOut

KitSeenOut.description: Who saw / approved a document, where (web | chat) and when.
KitSeenOut.title: KitSeenOut

KnownPeopleOut.description: known_people: `count` = every person found; `people` = at most KNOWN_PEOPLE_MAX; `truncated` = more exist.
KnownPeopleOut.title: KnownPeopleOut

KnownPersonOut.description:
One person the user already stored at this job's company (known_people). `company` is
the contact's own company, else its linked job's; `application_ids` = the jobs they are linked to.
KnownPersonOut.title: KnownPersonOut

LessonOut.description: One `lesson` event, read back across applications (slice 9, #516).
LessonOut.title: LessonOut

ListedPerson.description:
Outreach pack #15 — a person the ad itself names ("Meet the hiring team").
Stored as a contact on this application, found_via='job_ad'. Lengths and the
http(s) rule are add_contact's (contacts.validate_listed_people).
ListedPerson.title: ListedPerson

ListedPersonOut.description:
One per ``listed_people`` item, same order. ``error`` (closed set) = not stored:
"contact_cap" (CONTACTS_PER_APPLICATION_MAX) or "rate_limited" (CONTACTS_MAX_PER_HOUR).
ListedPersonOut.title: ListedPersonOut

MissingToolRequest.description:
``POST /api/missing-tools`` body. ``name`` must match
``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,59}$``; ``why`` is at most 280 characters.
MissingToolRequest.title: MissingToolRequest

NextStepOut.description:
What to do next on this application — a state machine over the stored
record (status, fit, CV versions, receipt, interview date, lesson), never
a judgement of the job. ``code`` is the closed vocabulary an agent
branches on; ``label`` is the sentence the web shows.
NextStepOut.title: NextStepOut

NormalizedOut.description:
One forgiving-input normalisation ``update_profile`` applied (owner decision 2026-10-10):
where it happened and a CLOSED rule code (``services/profile/forgiving.py``) - never a value.
NormalizedOut.title: NormalizedOut

OutreachCheckResponse.description:
The answer to "may I press Send on this outreach email?" - one gate
(``settings_rules.may_send_outreach``). ``send``: press Send in Gmail, then
record ``outreach_sent``; ``ask``: save a Gmail draft and ask_user; ``stop``:
do not send. ``sent_today`` / ``daily_max``: recorded sends today vs the cap.
OutreachCheckResponse.title: OutreachCheckResponse

OutreachEntryOut.description:
One row of a contact's outreach ledger — a drafted message VERSION
(``entry="message"``, ``version_no`` set) or a ``sent``/``reply`` mark
(``version_no`` null — unversioned, a person can be sent to or replied
to many times). Also a meeting/call/intro/referral entry (``follow_up_on``
is set only on those). A ``bounced`` mark's ``text`` is the address that bounced.
OutreachEntryOut.title: OutreachEntryOut

PayAdvertisedOut.description:
Pay exactly as the ad states it (job_checks.pay_facts). Never annualised:
``period`` is null when the ad does not say; ``currency`` is "UNKNOWN" when
no ISO code / unambiguous symbol sits beside the amount.
PayAdvertisedOut.title: PayAdvertisedOut

PersonFullOut.description:
``list_people(contact_id=...)``'s shape — the one row's own full
record (never merged with another row that happens to share an email).
PersonFullOut.title: PersonFullOut

PersonOut.description:
``list_people``'s no-``contact_id`` shape — one row per PERSON
(grouped by lower(email) else linkedin_url), aggregated across every
underlying ``application_contacts`` row that shares that identity.
PersonOut.title: PersonOut

ProfileEditExportOut.description:
One row of ``export_history``'s top-level ``profile_edits`` — EVERY
row, including a clear (``value: null``); it is the history, unlike
``GET /profile``'s ``agent_edits`` (the live, non-cleared overlay only).
ProfileEditExportOut.title: ProfileEditExportOut

ProfileEditHistoryRow.description:
One row of one field's history, newest first. ``value: null`` is a
clear (the field fell back to what the CV / the web form holds).
ProfileEditHistoryRow.title: ProfileEditHistoryRow

ProfileEditOut.description:
One row of the agent-edit overlay (slice 4, spec R8/R11).

The SAME shape everywhere an edit appears: ``GET /profile``'s
``agent_edits``, ``PATCH /profile``'s ``applied``, and
``export_history``'s ``profile_edits``. Declared once, here, so the
generated ``api-types.ts`` gives the frontend real field names instead of
the ``{[key: string]: unknown}[]`` an untyped ``dict`` renders as — the
profile page reads ``set_by`` and ``set_at`` off every one of these
(``components/profile/EditedMark.tsx``).

``value`` is ``Any``: the overlay carries whatever the path's dataclass
field holds — a string, a list of strings, a number, a bool.
ProfileEditOut.title: ProfileEditOut

ProfileVersionSummary.description:
One row in ``GET /profile/versions``. Mirrors the dict shape that
``services.profile.storage.list_profile_versions`` returns; CVData +
preferences blobs are passed through unmodified so the frontend can
diff snapshot-to-snapshot without an extra round-trip.
ProfileVersionSummary.title: ProfileVersionSummary

ProofMissingOut.description: An applied job with no proof yet; ``question``/``context`` go straight into ask_user.
ProofMissingOut.title: ProofMissingOut

ProofOut.description:
How well an application is backed up (S7): ``level`` is the strongest of
email > text > screenshot_only, else none - the one shape every surface reuses.
ProofOut.title: ProofOut

ReceiptAnswer.description:
One answer on a receipt. The SAME shape the ``form_filled`` event takes
(``kit.ANSWER_SOURCES`` is the one source list); ``source`` and ``key`` are
optional here, stored when given and returned on read.
ReceiptAnswer.title: ReceiptAnswer

ReceiptAnswerOut.description:
The READ shape of an answer — deliberately without the request caps.
A receipt is append-only history; if APPLICATION_RECEIPT_ANSWER_MAX_CHARS
is ever lowered, older rows must still read back, not 500 the page.
``source`` / ``key`` are absent on receipts recorded before they existed.
ReceiptAnswerOut.title: ReceiptAnswerOut

ReceiptFileOut.description:
Slice 29 - one file the receipt names: what Job360 uploaded or served (``document_uploaded``).
Slice 31 - or a file attached to the email (``event_id`` = the ``email_drafted``): then ``sha256`` is
of the artifact's TEXT and ``fmt`` is '' (the email's file format is not known).
ReceiptFileOut.title: ReceiptFileOut

ReceiptSummary.description: List row: everything but the three long bodies.
ReceiptSummary.title: ReceiptSummary

RecordOutreachRequest.description:
``POST /api/contacts/{contact_id}/outreach`` — the one shared door
``save_artifact``/``record_event`` (with a ``contact_id``) also call
(M5 parity).
RecordOutreachRequest.title: RecordOutreachRequest

message.default: Account request received. Please sign in to continue.

SaveFitLineOut.description:
Where the saved fit lands against the USER's own score line (owner

side uses (null when the side is unknown) and one plain next-step sentence.
SaveFitLineOut.title: SaveFitLineOut

SetVisaRequest.description:
Slice 7 — the human door (a person at the browser has no agent to
read the ad for them). Same three fields, same rules as bring_job /

SetVisaRequest.title: SetVisaRequest

SettingFieldOut.description:
One assistant setting: ``value`` as chosen ("" / null = not chosen),

SettingRequestExportOut.description: One setting-change request in the export: waiting or decided.

SettingRequestOut.title: SettingRequestOut

SetupProgressOut.description:

and the first unfinished one (``""`` when all are done).

StatsContactFoundViaGroupOut.description:
Owner decision 2026-10-04 — per current contact ``found_via``: how
many contacts, how many are ``reachable`` (CURRENT email or LinkedIn URL
saved), how many had an outreach marked sent / a reply recorded,
and ``reply_rate`` = contacts with both / contacts with a sent mark
(``null`` when nothing was sent).
StatsContactFoundViaGroupOut.title: StatsContactFoundViaGroupOut

StatsKeyedGroupOut.description:
Owner decision 2026-10-04 — ``by_country`` / ``by_job_source`` /
``by_channel``: same counts and rates as ``by_role``. ``key`` is the
canonical value (an ISO alpha-2 code or ``"remote"``; a closed-set

StatsKeyedGroupOut.title: StatsKeyedGroupOut

StatsOutreachVariantGroupOut.description:
Pack #13 — per outreach `label` (lower(trim)): contacts with a sent mark, counted
once under the label of their newest message version saved BEFORE their first sent
mark ('' / none = key null, "Not set"); of those, how many have a reply mark;
reply_rate = replied / sent; small_sample under STATS_SMALL_SAMPLE_N.
StatsOutreachVariantGroupOut.title: StatsOutreachVariantGroupOut

StatsPatternRowOut.description: One group of the ``patterns`` view (counts of the user's own sent applications).
StatsPatternRowOut.title: StatsPatternRowOut

StatsPatternsOut.description:
``stats(view="patterns")``. ``available`` false = below the gate (``text`` says
how far); every other key is then null.
StatsPatternsOut.title: StatsPatternsOut

StatsReferralsOut.description: ``stats(view="referrals")``: referred vs not. Facts only, never a ranking.
StatsReferralsOut.title: StatsReferralsOut

StatsScoreLineOut.description:
Owner decision 2026-10-10 - counts of the user's applications above /
below THEIR OWN score line (``line`` null = not set) and how many have no

StatsScoreLineOut.title: StatsScoreLineOut

StatsSitesOut.description: ``stats(view="sites")``: counts per form host. Facts only, never a ranking.

``stats(view="skill_gaps")``. ``available`` false = fewer than the threshold

StatsSkillGapsOut.title: StatsSkillGapsOut

SubmitCheckResponse.description:
The answer to "may I press submit on this application?" - one gate
(``settings_rules.may_submit``). ``submit``: go ahead; ``ask``: fill the form,
stop before submit and ask the user yes for this one; ``stop``: do not submit.
``reason`` is a closed code; ``detail`` is one plain sentence.
SubmitCheckResponse.title: SubmitCheckResponse

TailoredDocOut.description: One saved version of a tailored document — the newest of its kind.
TailoredDocOut.title: TailoredDocOut

TakeBackRequest.description:
``POST /profile/edits/take-back`` and ``/keep`` — the path whose
assistant edit the human takes back or keeps. ``extra="forbid"``: no way
to name another user.
TakeBackRequest.title: TakeBackRequest

UpdateContactRequest.description:
``PATCH /api/contacts/{contact_id}`` — every field optional; only the
ones given are appended to ``contact_edits`` (owner decision, 2026-09-25:
contacts ARE editable, old values kept). No length caps declared here —
same reasoning as ``AddContactRequest``: ``contacts.update_contact``
checks live ``settings`` values at call time.
UpdateContactRequest.title: UpdateContactRequest

UpdateJobFactsRequest.description:
Owner decision 2026-10-04 — set or fix the job's facts after
bring_job: ISO alpha-2 ``country``, ``remote``, ``found_on`` (closed set
JOB_FOUND_ON). Only the keys SENT change; an explicit ``null`` (or "")
clears one (rule #29: unset is null, never a default). Validated by
``job_facts.validate_job_facts`` — the same rules bring_job uses.
UpdateJobFactsRequest.title: UpdateJobFactsRequest

UpdateProfileResponse.description:
What ``PATCH /profile`` actually returns.

Declared as the route's ``response_model`` so the OpenAPI schema — and
therefore the frontend's generated ``api-types.ts`` — says so. An
undeclared ``dict[str, Any]`` return renders as a bare ``{}`` schema,
which tells a generated client nothing about the two keys it is about to
read (S2/N3).
UpdateProfileResponse.title: UpdateProfileResponse

WhatsNewEventOut.description:
``whats_new``'s raw event rows — no ``superseded`` (unlike
``ApplicationEventOut``); carries ``application_id`` instead.
WhatsNewEventOut.title: WhatsNewEventOut

post.description:
Gmail check slice (2026-10-15): move each application's ``inbox_checked_at``
cursor forward. The assistant read the mail; Job360 only remembers how far
(VISION rule 5). All or nothing; never rewinds a newer cursor.

get.description:
Read back an ad THIS user brought, by its `job_id`.

Slice 5 (#483) deleted the public `GET /api/jobs/{id}`. That route served
the shared catalog to anyone with an id, which stopped being defensible
the moment `jobs` held nothing but ads individual people pasted (S1). This
is its per-user replacement: the row is returned only when the caller has
an application for it, so an id they never brought reads as 404, never as
somebody else's paste.

Declared BEFORE `/applications/{application_id}` for the same reason
`/applications/export` is — a literal segment must not be swallowed by the
dynamic one.

Slice 9 (#516) — every "flag for next time" lesson across the caller's
applications, newest first (spec R1 door 1). Read-only; a lesson is
written through ``record_event`` (type ``lesson``) like any other event.
``get_profile`` carries the last PROFILE_LESSONS_MAX of the same list.

The fit picture (2026-09-20). Read-only; web only — an agent already
holds the profile and the ad (rule M2), so there is no MCP tool.

post.description:
Verify or Edit one answer on a ready card (owner decision 2026-10-18): it is
saved as the user's own word in memory, so the assistant uses it next time.
Session only - an assistant can never vouch for its own answer. Returns the
card again; 404 / 409 (the fill changed) / 422 write nothing. Logs paths only.

get.description:
Slice 8 (#515) — original vs tailored, read-only (spec R1). No Keep:
the version the receipt names is the applied one (decision 26).

parameters.description: `profile` (the stored CV text) or another artifact id of the same kind. Default: `profile` for a cv, the previous version otherwise.
parameters.name: against

schema.description: `profile` (the stored CV text) or another artifact id of the same kind. Default: `profile` for a cv, the previous version otherwise.
schema.title: Against

post.description:
Render ONE stored CV / cover-letter version as PDF or DOCX (web-only —
the agent already holds the text). POST like the tailor download so it is
Origin-checked; it writes nothing. Foreign application/artifact -> 404.

get.description:
THE one gate before an automatic employer email (feedback loop slice 2).

``kind``: checkin | feedback_request | feedback_followup. Answers ``send`` / ``ask`` / ``stop`` with a
closed ``reason`` through ``auto_emails.decide`` (the same function for this route and the MCP
``check_auto_email`` tool). ``send`` only means the gate is open. Read-only apart from one audit line.
404 for an application that is not the caller's (rule #12).

post.description:
"Autofill" / "Don't autofill" - may the assistant type into this form at
all. Latest wins; unset means the assistant follows its own app permission.

"Mark resolved" - the user sorted out what stopped their assistant: records
``unblocked`` {resolution: user_did_it} and closes the blocked ask. 409 when
nothing is blocked. Session only; assistants use ``record_event``.

"I submitted it" - the user got past the block and pressed Submit themselves:
records ``unblocked`` {resolution: user_did_it} (as "Mark resolved" does) and the
receipt (``recorded_by`` web, the pasted confirmation), in ONE transaction. 409 when
nothing is blocked, or when the application already has a receipt or is no longer
``considering`` (check_submit's ``already_applied``); nothing is written then.
Session only; assistants use ``record_event`` + ``record_application``.

get.description: One application's interview and follow-up, as a download (Add to calendar).

post.description:
201 for a new contact, 200 (``already_existed: true``, ``matched_on``)
for the same person seen again on this application (R2): same email, else
(no email) same normalised LinkedIn URL, else same phone (7+ digits), else same name unless
both carry different LinkedIn URLs or phones; also a repeated ``client_key``. The status code is
set dynamically since the same call can legitimately answer either.

get.description:
What the four buttons on the application page show: is the latest CV seen /
approved (who, where, when), did the user say don't send, the autofill choice,
and the duplicate warning. Read-only.

post.description:
"I've checked this CV" - the user's own click records ``cv_seen`` (where=web)
for the latest CV, once per version. Session only; no MCP twin.

"Not a duplicate, go ahead" - clears the duplicate-job ask and the unattended
duplicate stop for THIS application. Web only.

"Release" - the user frees an application another assistant session holds (it crashed
or was closed): appends ``hold_released`` {reason: stopped, by: web}; nothing is rewritten.
``{released: false}`` and no event when no hold is live. 404 for an application that is not
the caller's. Session only: a bearer token is refused, so an assistant can never release
another session's hold; assistants record ``hold_released`` through ``record_event``.

patch.description:
The web job page's door, and the ``update_job`` MCP tool's route.
Writes the caller's OWN application row only (never the shared ``jobs``
catalog — hard rule #10); a foreign/unknown id reads 404 (S2).

get.description:
The application kit (S3): the CV and cover letter of THIS application, every
stored answer with its source, what is missing for the job's country, fresh
30-minute file links, the duplicate / hold / account-site / autofill state and
the gate's preview. Writes one ``kit_read`` event (the timeline shows who read
it and when) and one link row per document; the file tokens appear only in this
response. 404 for an application that is not the caller's; 429 over the
hourly cap. Document ``text`` is cut to ``KIT_DOC_TEXT_MAX_CHARS`` (``text_truncated`` /
``text_more``; ``include_text=false`` sends none); ``approved_text`` keeps the newest
``KIT_APPROVED_TEXT_MAX`` (``answers_omitted``). ``session`` is the assistant
session's own short label (``kit.clean_session``; 422 otherwise): it is stored on
the ``kit_read`` so ``hold`` can tell two sessions of one assistant apart.
``Cache-Control: no-store``.

post.description:
Which questions on the LIVE form already have a saved answer. The assistant reads
the form, lists every question (optional ones too, ``required=false``) and, for each,
the kit ``key`` it plans to use. Job360 checks that key really exists in THIS
application's kit (an ``approved_text`` answer also matches by its question); with no
key it matches the normalized wording of the question against the user's approved
answers. No fuzzy matching, no NLP. ``answered`` carries the value and its source
(``confirmed: false`` = inferred, confirm with the user); ``missing`` is what to ask
the user, once. Each question may also carry the live control's ``field_type``, ``options``,
``limit`` and ``limit_unit``: a saved value outside ``options`` is a gap, one over ``limit``
is flagged ``over_limit`` (never cut), sensitive questions are flagged ``needs_confirmation``
and knock-out questions are listed in ``knockouts`` with ``stop_for_user``. Read-only: no event is
written. 404 for an application that is not the
caller's. ``Cache-Control: no-store``.

get.description: Proof level plus screenshots.

post.description: Mint a one-time upload link for THIS application's proof screenshot (5 minutes).

"Send this one" - the user says yes to sending this application with the
latest CV. Records ``cv_seen`` (if not already) then ``submit_approved``, both
where=web. A CV edited later makes the yes stop matching; slice 8: so does a new
letter, fill, form page or assistant profile edit, or SUBMIT_APPROVAL_TTL_MINUTES passing
or a newer ``email_drafted`` with another recipient or attachment (slice 31; ``fingerprint`` on the
event; check_submit asks ``approval_stale``). Clears an earlier
"don't send". S5d: ``artifact_id`` / ``form_filled_event_id`` name the CV and
the fill the user was looking at; when either is no longer the newest, 409 and
nothing is recorded (the yes must name what the user saw).

"Don't send" - the gate answers ``stop`` / ``user_declined`` until a later
"Send this one".

get.description:
THE one gate before a final submit (owner decision 2026-10-08, S2).

Reads the user's settings, this application's own facts (status, receipt,
the per-job override) and the day's counts, then answers through
``settings_rules.may_submit`` - the same function for every caller (this route
and the MCP ``check_submit`` tool). ``form_url`` is the address of the page
the form is on (a bare host works too); without it the answer is ``ask``
(``unknown_site``). The address is read strictly (``screen_form_url``): a
user-info ``@``, ``%`` or backslash in the authority, a non-ASCII / IDNA host
or a non-http(s) scheme answers ``ask`` / ``unknown_site``, and a host other
than the newest ``form_filled``'s answers ``ask`` / ``form_host_mismatch``, and a
host + path other than the page stored on the newest ``form_filled`` / ``form_swept``
(``kit.latest_form_url``) answers ``ask`` / ``form_page_mismatch`` - a stored yes
clears none of them. An EMAIL application passes ``form_url=mailto:<to>`` (slice 31, G078): no form
rules, but ``stop`` / ``email_not_drafted`` until an ``email_drafted`` to that address is recorded.
An unconfirmed email answers ``ask`` /
``email_not_verified``. ``session`` is the caller's own label (the one it gave
``get_application_kit``; 422 when malformed): another session's live kit hold
answers ``ask`` / ``held_by_other_session``, which a yes does not clear (only
``hold_released`` or the end of ``KIT_HOLD_MINUTES`` does). Read-only. 404 for an
application that is not the caller's (rule #12).

post.description:
The user confirms a relayed chat answer. Web session only: an assistant
can never confirm for the user, so there is deliberately no MCP tool.

Take an open ask back. The user (web) may withdraw any ask, reason optional. An assistant
(the MCP ``answer_ask`` ``withdraw``) may withdraw only an ask it asked itself, and must say why
(owner, 2026-10-23); an ask the user or another assistant raised stays the user's to close.

get.description:
The caller's settings (each raw + effective), the practice-run state and
the requests waiting for the user's OK. Read-only; any signed-in caller.

Every change to ONE setting, newest first, both sides (the user's web
rows and the assistant's). At most ``PROFILE_EDIT_HISTORY_MAX`` rows.

post.description:
The user confirms a waiting request: the change is applied now as a WEB
row (so history says the human did it). 404 when the id is not the caller's;
409 when it was already decided or has expired; 422 when the stored value no
longer passes validation (for example a pause time that has since passed).

The user declines a waiting request ("Don't change"): nothing is applied
and the request is closed. Same 404 / 409 rules as confirm.

Put one setting back to what it held BEFORE its newest change.

Append-only: a new ``web`` row carries the value of the row before the
newest one (``null`` — the safe default — when there was none). Not
rate-limited (the human's own action). 404 when the setting never changed.

schema.title: Response Delete Trigger Api Assistant Trigger Delete

get.description: Is Send set to start the user's assistant? Host and last result only; never the token.

schema.title: Response Get Trigger Api Assistant Trigger Get

put.description:
Save (or replace) the start address and its token. The token is encrypted at rest.

An unexpected error must not carry the plaintext token into an error report: the body is emptied of
it, the error is logged without its traceback or message, and a plain 500 replaces it (from None).

schema.title: Response Put Trigger Api Assistant Trigger Put

post.description:
Called by the website right after Send / Send all: start the user's assistant once for every
application whose newest send decision is their yes. Never fails the Send itself: a problem comes
back as ``fired: false`` with a reason the page shows.

schema.title: Response Fire Trigger Api Assistant Trigger Fire Post

post.description:
Undo an email change from the link mailed to the OLD address.

Public, authenticated by its one-time token (like password-reset/confirm).
On success: 204, the previous email and its previous verified state are
back, and every session, agent token and OAuth grant is revoked.
Unknown, used, expired or deleted-user token: generic 400. The previous
address now belonging to another account: 409, nothing changed.

Rate-limited per IP (429) like the password-reset request.

Validate a magic-link token, sign the user in (find-or-create + verify).

On success sets the session cookie and returns the user. On any failure
(unknown / expired / already-used token) raises 400 with a generic
message so token existence can't be probed.

Email a passwordless sign-in link.

Always returns 204 regardless of whether the email is registered — the
account is created lazily on consume, so there's nothing to enumerate.
Rate-limited to 3 requests per 5 minutes per email so an attacker can't
spam any address with sign-in emails. When limited we still return 204
(indistinguishable) but issue no token and send no email.

put.description:
Web session only: the user's own "Help improve Job360" switch (gap roadmap slice 4).

The ONE write door for `users.analytics_consent_at`. ``true`` stamps when they
agreed; ``false`` clears it, which withdraws consent at once (server PostHog
capture and Sentry session replay both read it). Consent is the person's own
choice, so an assistant's token is refused (403 ``session_required``).

get.description: Cheap read for the dashboard to render a 'verify email' banner.

schema.title: Response Get Email Verified Api Auth Me Email Verified Get

put.description:
Web session only (security review 2026-10-18): the user's timezone sets their day, week and
``apply_hours``, so an assistant's token must not move it.

Owner decision, 2026-09-25 — the ONE write door for `users.timezone`
(browser-prefilled on the account settings page, but only ever SAVED
here, on an explicit press — rule #29). A name `ZoneInfo` cannot resolve
is refused with 422 naming the bad value; a valid one is stored and used
by `spine.user_today` for every "what's due today" read from then on.

post.description:
Validate the token and set the new password.

On success: 204, and every existing session, agent token and OAuth grant
for that user is revoked (forces re-login on all devices and reconnection
of every assistant — security best practice after reset).
The caller's session cookie is cleared too so the API response itself
can't accidentally land the caller into the just-reset account.

On failure: 400 with a generic message. We deliberately don't
distinguish unknown vs expired vs used vs deleted-user — that would
leak which tokens exist.

Initiate a password-reset email.

Always returns 204 regardless of whether the email is registered —
no-enumeration contract (per OWASP). The service layer logs the
distinction internally for ops.

**Rate-limited** (Phase −2 review fix #3): 1 request per minute per
IP. When limited, returns 204 *without* issuing a token or sending
an email — preserves the no-enumeration contract by being
indistinguishable from "unknown email" responses. Logged so an
operator can see the suppression pattern.

delete.description:
ERASE the caller's account (GDPR Article 17), then clear the session cookie.

Web session only: an agent token can never erase the account. An account
with a password must send it (hard rule #26). An account with NO password
(``has_password`` FALSE: only a magic link ever signed it in) cannot, so it
may delete only from a session created by a fresh email link, inside
``ACCOUNT_DELETE_FRESH_SESSION_SECONDS``; otherwise 403 says how.

Uses hard_delete_user (docs/fable/05) — actually erases all per-user data
(CV, profile, channels, feed, actions, …), not a soft `deleted_at` flag that
left the data in place and could be resurrected on a later magic-link consume.

patch.description:
Change email. Requires current password. Invalidates session → re-login required.

The new address is unproven, so ``email_verified_at`` is cleared and the
verification mail goes to it. The OLD address gets a notice with a 24 h
one-time link that undoes the change (``/email-change/undo``). Both mails
are background work: a failed send never breaks the request.

get.description:
Download everything we hold on the caller as one JSON file (Article 20).

Web session only (gap roadmap slice 3): a leaked, never-expiring agent token
must not be able to download the whole account. An assistant reads history
through ``export_history``, which leaves out the account tables.

GET is correct here: it is a pure read, no state changes. Scoped to the
session's own ``user.id`` (rule #12) — the caller can never name another user.
Secrets (password hash, encrypted channel creds) are redacted and the
security-token tables are omitted entirely; see ``export_user_data``.

patch.description:
Authenticated password change. Requires current password verification,
then invalidates the session cookie to force re-login (hard rule #26 —
matches the email-change path).

post.description:
Validate token and mark the user's email verified.

No session required — the link in the email is the authentication
artefact. Returns 204 on success, 400 on any failure (generic to
prevent token-existence enumeration).

Resend the verification email for the current user.

Requires an active session — there's no public 'resend by email
address' endpoint because that would let an attacker spam any
address. Repeated requests issue independently-valid tokens (any of
the unused ones works until its own expiry), so the user can't lock
themselves out by hitting resend twice.

**Rate-limited** (Phase −2 review fix #3): 1 request per minute per
user. The session-gate already bounds the threat (only authenticated
users can call), but a frustrated user clicking resend rapidly would
burn through SMTP quota. Returns HTTP 429 when limited; UX should
surface the cooldown.

One action in the caller's cloud browser (open, look, click, type, choose, tick, upload, back,
close). Refusals come back as ``status`` + ``reason`` + ``detail`` with HTTP 200, so an assistant
reads them like any page; a 404 from the gate (not the caller's application) stays a 404.

schema.title: Response Browser Action Api Browser Post

post.description:
One step of the user signing in to a job site themselves: start (url), shot, click (x, y),
type (text), key, scroll (dy), keep, cancel. Returns a picture of the page. Typed text is never
logged or returned; the audit line names the action only. ``mode: finish``: the user finishes a
human check in their assistant's browser instead (shot, click, type, key, scroll, done).

schema.title: Response Browser Live Api Browser Live Post

get.description: The job sites the user's cloud browser is kept signed in to (never a cookie value).

schema.title: Response List Sign Ins Api Browser Sign Ins Get

delete.description: Forget one saved sign-in. The user's browsers (if any) are closed so they forget too.

schema.title: Response Forget Sign In Api Browser Sign Ins  Host  Delete

post.description:
Create the feed, or rotate it (the old URL dies). The plain URL is in this
response only; the database keeps the hash.

get.description: Serve the feed. See the module docstring for the rules.

post.description: Record a browser-side log event into the server's data/logs/ stream.

Owner decision, 2026-09-25 — a person with no job yet (cold
networking), or a linked one when ``application_id`` is given. Same
idempotency/cap/rate-limit rules as the per-application route, just
scoped to the USER instead of an application when there is none. Cold
scope without an email: same LinkedIn URL, else same phone (7+ digits),
else same name only when neither side has a LinkedIn URL or a phone. ``source_url`` is stored, never fetched.

Many people in one call: ``dry_run`` previews ``would_add`` /
``duplicates`` / ``invalid`` by index and writes nothing; without it each
person is stored in its own transaction (idempotent, like ``add_contact``).
A bad row lands in ``invalid`` and never fails the rest. Status 200 always.

patch.description:
Owner decision, 2026-09-25 — contacts ARE editable, old values kept:
every provided field appends a ``contact_edits`` row (S12 — the base row
is never touched); the response is the CURRENT view (base + latest edit
per field) plus the full history. A foreign/unknown id reads 404 (S2).

post.description: The user's own Confirm on a person their assistant added. Session only; no MCP twin.

The one shared door for a contact's outreach ledger — a drafted
message VERSION, or a ``sent``/``reply`` mark. ``save_artifact``
(``kind="outreach"`` + ``contact_id``) and ``record_event``
(``outreach_sent``/``outreach_replied`` + ``contact_id``) both delegate to
the SAME service function this route calls (M5 parity) — this route is
the one door that works for a COLD contact too, since it carries no
``application_id`` in its URL. A ``client_key`` lives in the key space of
the tool that calls this door: ``save_artifact`` for a message version,
``record_event`` for a sent/reply mark.

get.description:
THE one gate before pressing Send on an outreach email (feature 10).

Reads the user's settings (``assistant_settings.outreach_send`` decides send vs
ask; the Gmail mode never does), this contact's facts and the saved message
version ``message_id`` (the ``contact_outreach`` row ``save_artifact
kind="outreach"`` created), plus today's recorded sends, then answers
through ``settings_rules.may_send_outreach`` - the same function for this
route and the MCP ``check_outreach`` tool. Read-only: it records nothing
except one audit line. 404 for a contact that is not the caller's (rule #12).

Deploy healthcheck (2026-10-22): readyz's DB check, then the browser hold.

A new container answers 503 ``holding`` while the OLD process still has a recently active
cloud browser, for at most ``DEPLOY_HOLD_MAX_SECONDS`` after this process booted, so Railway
keeps the old container (and its half-filled form) serving. See
``services/browser_agent/deploy_hold.py``. Public, since Railway's healthcheck sends no
credentials; the body carries no user data and no counts.

200 ``{"status": "ready"}``
503 ``{"status": "not_ready", "reason": "pool_timeout" | "db_error"}`` (wins over the hold)
503 ``{"status": "holding", "reason": "browser_busy", "held_s": <seconds since boot>}``

The account's state in one read, plus ONE closed ``next_step``:
``verify_email | upload_cv | setup:<round> | answer_asks | confirm_settings | ok``.
Read-only except the auto-ghost sweep (a `ghosted` event per silent
application, reported in ghosted_now); email verification is NOT required (an unverified user is told
to verify). No 404 when there is no profile (``profile_exists: false``).

Also the MCP tool list as served now (``tools``, ``tools_version``) so an
assistant can tell its client cached an old one: pass the version it saw
last as ``client_tools_version`` and ``tools_stale`` says whether it moved
(null when none was passed).
Serve one kit file. See the module docstring for the rules.
The kit's files with size and SHA-256, so the assistant can check what it ran.
One kit file. Unknown names are 404 and never touch the filesystem.

post.description:
Store the pasted ad and birth the Application for it.

Nothing is scored: the caller (the user's agent) already decided this ad
is worth keeping, and product rule 4 forbids us judging fit. Returns the
stored job plus the `application_id` the caller should work against from
here on. A repeated ``client_key`` returns the first reply (slice 25).

Fetch a job-ad URL the user pasted, under the SSRF guard, and hand
back extracted fields for the form to pre-fill. Never stores anything
(S2) — the human still presses "Score this job" to actually bring it.

Always HTTP 200 with a closed ``outcome`` except auth (401), the feature
switch (404), a rate limit (429), or a malformed body (422) — "the site
refused us" is a product outcome the form renders a sentence for, not a
transport error (spec R1).

get.description:
Liveness probe — returns 200 as long as the process is running.

No dependency checks. Kubernetes/Railway liveness must not fail because
the DB momentarily blipped; that is what /readyz is for.

post.description:
Store "a tool I needed does not exist" for the owner. It only stores.
422 when ``name`` is not ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,59}$`` or ``why`` is over 280
characters (the message names the rule, never the value); 429 past
``MISSING_TOOL_REPORTS_MAX_PER_DAY`` reports in the last 24 hours.

get.description: State + the four-bucket tally since ``since``.

No ``contact_id`` — every person the user has added, grouped by
lower(email) else linkedin_url (the same recruiter on two jobs is one
person here). With ``contact_id`` — that ONE row's own full record
(message versions, sent/reply marks, detail-edit history), never merged.
``company`` keeps only people whose company (or linked job's company) has the same company key as jobs (rule #1).

Return the caller's profile summary.

Per-user storage landed in Batch 3.5.2 — each user has their own row
in ``user_profiles`` keyed by ``user.id``. No more silent overwrites
between authenticated users.

patch.description:
Apply 1..N agent edits to the caller's profile as one atomic overlay write.

R12 — the same function REST and MCP call: the MCP `update_profile` tool
invokes this route function directly with the resolved user (the pattern
every other MCP tool in `mcp_server.py` already uses), so there is
exactly one place this logic can drift.

All-or-nothing (S12): every edit is validated before anything is
written — one bad path or value means the whole call 422s and NOTHING
changes. A user with no profile row yet gets an empty base created first
(R8) so the overlay has something to sit on. The response carries the
full merged profile (`GET /profile`'s own shape) so the caller sees the
effect without a second round trip.

The audit line for this action names PATHS and the actor only — never a
value (S3): an edit can carry a name, an email fragment inside `about_me`,
or anything else the agent chose to write, and none of that belongs in a
log line.

Gap 4 (slice 26) - two assistants writing one profile: the whole call runs
under the user's profile-write lock, so `expected_profile_version` (409
`stale_profile` when another write landed since) and the item ops (applied
to the CURRENT list) are checked against exactly what gets written.

post.description:
Combined CV + preferences (backward-compatible with the frontend form).

The dedicated single-input routes are POST /profile/cv and
POST /profile/preferences; this endpoint accepts both together.

Loads the BASE profile (``with_overlay=False``) for the same reason the
dedicated routes do — it mutates and saves.

Empty ONE input (or the whole profile), so the next upload starts clean.

WEB SESSION ONLY (gap roadmap slice 3): "all" wipes the CV, preferences,
memory and assistant settings at once, so a leaked agent token must not
reach it. An assistant clears one field with ``update_profile(null)``.

``section``: cv | linkedin | github | preferences | memory | all.

``memory`` (owner decision 2026-10-08) empties ONLY the user-info memory
(``user_info.*``: contact, right to work, logistics, languages, equality
answers, saved answers): the base column and the assistant's overlay rows.
It takes no version snapshot (it copies the memory into ``profile_edits``
first instead, ``_snapshot_memory_then_clear``) and leaves the CV, the
preferences and ``daily_check`` alone. ``preferences`` leaves the memory alone (and clears
``salary_by_country`` with the other job preferences); ``cv`` / ``linkedin`` /
``github`` leave it alone; only ``all`` resets it.

Deliberately does NOT re-run extraction: there is nothing left to read, so
rebuilding an emptied profile would be pure waste. The stored snapshot taken
by ``save_profile`` is what makes this reversible.

CLEARS THE AGENT'S EDITS TOO. The overlay sits ON TOP of the stored
profile, so emptying only the base left every agent edit in the cleared
scope still showing on the page — the button said "Clear" and the value
stayed. Worse, the overlay is what "Clear" exists to remove before a
fresh upload: the whole point is a clean experiment. So each cleared
scope also appends a clearing row (``value = NULL``, append-only) for
every overlay path it covers: ``cv`` -> ``cv_data.*``, ``preferences``
-> ``preferences.*``, ``memory`` -> ``user_info.*``, ``all`` -> all three.
``linkedin`` and ``github`` own no editable path, so they clear nothing in
the overlay.

Set the caller's CV (PDF/DOCX) — one input, one dedicated route.

Loads the BASE profile (``with_overlay=False``): this route MUTATES and
SAVES, and starting from the merged profile would copy the agent's
overlay values into the extraction's own JSON — see the note on
``storage.load_profile``.

get.description:
Every change to ONE of the caller's profile fields, newest first.

Both sides in one list: the human's own web saves (``set_by: "web"``) and
the assistant's edits (``agent:…`` / ``token:…``); ``value: null`` is a
clear. At most ``PROFILE_EDIT_HISTORY_MAX`` rows — ``export_history``
carries the whole log. Scoped to the caller (rule #12): the query filters
by ``user.id``, so no parameter can reach another user's rows.

post.description:
Keep the assistant's change to one field: the human accepts it as theirs.

Writes the assistant's CURRENT value into the BASE profile, then appends
a row with that same value authored by the caller (``web`` in a browser).
The newest row is now the human's, so the mark goes, and a later "Take
back" has nothing to undo (404) — the value is the human's own now, and
survives any later autosave or re-extraction of the overlay.

Append-only (M3): the assistant's row stays in the history. Not
rate-limited (the human's own action). No MCP tool: an assistant cannot
accept its own edit on the user's behalf. 404 when the field has no live
assistant edit; the lookup is scoped by ``user.id`` (rule #12).

Take back the assistant's change to one field: it falls back to the
value from the CV / the web form (the base profile).

Append-only (M3): a new clearing row (``value = NULL``) authored by the
caller — ``web`` for a signed-in human; the assistant's row stays in the
history. NOT rate-limited, same as the section clear: the human undoing
an assistant must never spend the assistant's edit budget.

404 when the field's newest row is not a live assistant edit — there is
nothing to take back (and a caller can never name another user's field:
the lookup is scoped by ``user.id``).

Enrich the caller's profile with GitHub public data.

Accepts a full profile URL or @handle, not just a bare username —
``normalize_github_username`` reduces it to the handle before lookup.

FAILS LOUDLY (2026-08-08). This route used to return ``ok=True, merged=True``
unconditionally, so a handle that reduced to nothing still produced a green
"GitHub profile enriched" toast — and, once receipts shipped, a "GitHub
connected" row on the profile page — while zero repos were read. Measured on
a live profile: ``github_connected_at`` stamped, ``github_username`` empty,
0 repos. A receipt that confirms something that did not happen is worse than
no receipt at all.

A handle that does not reduce to a valid GitHub username is a 400 with
wording the person can act on. ``normalize_github_username`` accepts a bare
handle, an @handle, a profile URL, and a ``<user>.github.io`` Pages URL
(whose subdomain IS the username — a CV lists that under "Portfolio", so it
is exactly what people paste here).

get.description:
Step-1.5 S3-C — export the caller's CV as a JSON Resume document
(https://jsonresume.org/schema/). Wraps the existing
``CVData.to_json_resume()`` helper Batch 1.8 shipped — additive,
read-only, no rename of internal fields. 404 when the caller has no
profile row yet.

post.description:
Enrich user profile with a LinkedIn 'Save to PDF' profile export.

WHAT A SUCCESSFUL UPLOAD MEANS (decision 28, 2026-09-21). Job360 stores the
export's TEXT — that is the deliverable, because the user's own agent reads
it (`get_profile`) and writes the sections back (`update_profile`). So a
file that IS a LinkedIn export and yields text is a 200; the rejection
happens BEFORE any profile field is touched, when the text does not look
like an export at all.

Success used to mean "did a model find skills or positions in it"
(`bool(cv.linkedin_skills or cv.linkedin_positions)`, checked after
extraction, 422 otherwise). That was right while Job360 did the reading and
is wrong now: an export whose Top-Skills sidebar is collapsed would be
rejected and its text — the thing the agent actually needs — thrown away.

The reset before the re-read is SCOPED to the structural fields this route
can rewrite. The prose sections (positions, courses, honors, …) belong to
the agent and are never cleared, because nothing here could refill them.

Set the caller's preferences form — one input, one dedicated route.

Loads the BASE profile (``with_overlay=False``) and, after saving,
appends a ``set_by=web`` history row for every preference the human
actually changed — see :func:`_record_web_preference_changes`.

get.description:
Step-1.5 S3-A — list the most-recent ``user_profile_versions`` rows
for the caller, newest first. Each save_profile() also writes a
snapshot here (Pillar 1 Batch 1.8) so the list is non-empty whenever
the user has at least one profile save.

Returns 200 with an empty ``versions`` array when the user has no
profile yet — preferred over 404 because the UI history page can
render a "no versions yet" state from the empty list.

Return per-field differences between two profile versions, scoped to caller.

Step-3 B-10. Compares cv_data JSON blobs from both versions. Only fields
that differ are included in ``changes``. Returns 404 when either version is
missing or belongs to another user (existence-hiding).

Tenant-scoped: ``restore_profile_version`` returns ``None`` when the

get.description:
The caller's ready-to-send cards, newest fill first. ``limit=0`` = counts
only. ``application_id`` narrows it to one (404 when it is not the caller's).

Readiness probe: can the request path get a DB connection right now?

Production borrows a connection from the SAME pool ``get_request_db`` uses
(``repositories/pool.py``), waiting at most ``READYZ_POOL_TIMEOUT_S``, and
runs ``SELECT 1`` under the same bound. A pinned pool (every connection
held) or an unreachable database answers 503, which is what Railway's deploy
healthcheck (``backend/railway.json``) and the uptime probe need to see.

200 ``{"status": "ready", "pool": {size, idle, used, waiting, max}}``
503 ``{"status": "not_ready", "reason": "pool_timeout" | "db_error"}``

Test mode has no request-path pool (``get_request_db`` opens a fresh
connection per request there), so the probe opens one the same way and
``pool`` is null. Redis is no longer checked: the service was deleted
2026-09-02 and the auth rate limiter falls back without it.

"I applied": freeze the receipt, then mark the job applied on the
application spine's `applications` row so every surface agrees.

response; the public-audit fix then removed ``jobs_total`` — a public

The newest saved CV and cover letter for this job (empty list if the

Save the user's own edit as a NEW version (guardrail #3 — always
editable). Nothing is overwritten: the agent's version and every earlier
edit stay readable forever (M3), and the edit is stamped ``made_by="human"``.

post.description:
Download the newest saved version as an ATS-friendly PDF or DOCX.

``fmt`` = ``pdf`` (default) | ``docx``.

POST, not GET (docs/fable/01 S6): this endpoint MUTATES — it feeds
`_learn_universal`. A side-effecting GET is both wrong HTTP semantics and a
CSRF hole: `OriginCheckMiddleware` only guards unsafe methods, and a
cross-site top-level link click still sends the SameSite=Lax cookie. As POST
it is Origin-checked like every other mutation. The frontend already fetches
this as a blob, so the method is transparent there.

"This is the one I'm using" — the learning trigger (§5 learn-from-kept-only).

Writes nothing to the document: the version history IS the record (decision
26 — no Keep flag on an artifact). All it does is record the STRUCTURE of the
kept text in the universal patterns store (§7 privacy — never content).

get.description:
Per-line provenance for the newest saved version: which lines are the
user's OWN facts (grounded in their profile), which only echo the job ad
(``source="ad"``: employer context, never a candidate fact) and which were added.
Deterministic, no LLM — shown before download so the user can verify what is
real (guardrail #2).

get.description:
The commit this process was deployed from (2026-10-20).

post-merge-watch.yml polls this until it reports the merge SHA, so "deployed"
means THIS commit is serving, not that the old container still answers 200
(readyz and /health cannot tell the two apart). Railway injects
RAILWAY_GIT_COMMIT_SHA on every GitHub deploy, and a rollback restores the old
deployment's variables, so after a rollback this reports the old SHA. Public and
data-free: the SHA is already public on GitHub. ``no-store`` so no proxy can
serve an old SHA after the swap.
